tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local fixture for O5,D5,I5. A provider terminal proof P_old was minted while repository claim/fence F5 was authoritative. P_old is immutably bound to exact O5,D5,I5, guarantees complete history, permanent sealed/quiescent terminality, and explicit no-effect attestation for every covered attempt. Later repository claim/fence F6 becomes authoritative for the same exact O5,D5,I5, without changing provider identity or reopening provider execution. Test only whether P_old must itself be minted under F6 to support repository terminal negative closure, assuming finalization still requires current F6 CAS and exact readback. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

premises: P_old is immutably bound to exact O5,D5,I5.
P_old attests complete provider attempt history for O5,D5,I5.
P_old attests permanent sealed/quiescent terminality: no attempt for O5,D5,I5 can be created, resumed, or executed after the proof snapshot.
P_old explicitly attests that no covered attempt crossed the irreversible-effect boundary.
The later repository fence F6 does not alter O5,D5,I5, does not reopen provider execution, and cannot invalidate provider sealing.
Repository finalization under F6 still requires current-claim CAS and exact readback.
fixture.candidate_action: F6 accepts P_old as provider-side terminal no-effect evidence and records repository terminal negative closure only through current F6 CAS/readback.
fixture.reason: Under these premises, freshness of the repository claim epoch and validity of the provider terminal proof are separate obligations. P_old already proves the provider-side fact for the unchanged exact identity O5,D5,I5 and remains valid because sealing is permanent and no later claim can create new provider work. Requiring the proof to be minted under F6 adds no safety information. Repository authority freshness is instead enforced by F6 CAS/readback. The conclusion fails if a new claim can rotate provider identity, reopen execution, invalidate sealing, or otherwise change the provider-side proof domain.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: Even when a provider proof is exact-identity-bound, complete, permanently sealed, and explicitly attests no irreversible effect, it cannot be used after a later repository claim/fence becomes authoritative unless the provider remints the proof under that current repository claim epoch.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: For unchanged O5,D5,I5 with permanent provider sealing, the provider fact proven by P_old does not change when repository authority advances from F5 to F6. Current repository authority is separately protected by F6 CAS/readback, so claim-epoch co-minting is not necessary in this exact scope.

minimum_safe_conditions: Provider proof is immutably bound to exact O5,D5,I5.
Provider history is complete for that identity.
Provider terminality is permanently sealed/quiescent across repository claim changes.
Explicit no-effect attestation covers every attempt in that complete history.
Later repository claims cannot rotate identity, reopen execution, or invalidate sealing without producing a different proof domain.
Repository finalization uses the current authoritative fence F6 with CAS and exact readback.

observations: Provider-proof freshness and repository-claim freshness are distinct safety dimensions when the provider proof domain is immutable and permanently sealed.
Binding a provider proof to the exact operation/payload/idempotency identity can be sufficient without binding its mint time to the current repository claim epoch.
The separation is unsafe if a later claim can change provider identity or reopen provider execution.
inference: Within this exact fixture, an earlier provider terminal no-effect proof remains sufficient after repository claim advancement when its identity domain is unchanged, its terminal seal is permanent, and current repository authority is enforced independently by F6 CAS/readback. Current-epoch reminting is not intrinsically required; domain continuity and permanent sealing are the critical conditions.
